name: Bhamaha
dates_notes: Bhāmaha is generally placed in the seventh century by relative textual chronology; neither precise dates nor a secure biography are available.
core_thesis: Bhāmaha is among the earliest extant systematic theorists of Sanskrit poetics. His *Kāvyālaṅkāra* treats poetry through the interdependence of word and meaning, while giving figures of speech, poetic defects, and compositional judgement a central analytical role. He should not be reduced to the later textbook label of an ornament-only theorist: the work also addresses the conditions under which expression is intelligible, apt, and aesthetically effective. It establishes an early technical vocabulary against which later theorists of style, suggestion, and rasa formulate their alternatives.

engaged_works.title: Kavyalankara
engaged_works.composition_dates_notes: Conventionally dated to the seventh century by its place in the early history of Sanskrit poetics.
engaged_works.ascription_notes: The extant treatise is securely transmitted and studied as Bhāmaha's work.

ascription_evidence.description: Modern histories of Sanskrit poetics treat the Kāvyālaṅkāra as Bhāmaha's extant work.

engaged_works.summary: An early systematic treatise on Sanskrit poetics, conventionally divided into six chapters. It surveys the nature of poetry, poetic defects, figures of speech, and standards of verbal and semantic fitness. The work is a major source for the early alaṅkāra tradition and for later debates over what makes a text poetic.
